newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty genl seeks registration of beer kegs.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty genl seeks registration of beer kegs.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on Friday urged state lawmakers to approve a bill requiring anyone who buys a keg of beer to register it.
The bill would require package stores and grocery stores with beer permits to place identification tags on beer kegs, and require buyers to sign a receipt.
Blumenthal said the measure would deter underage drinking.
"Keg registration can help eradicate drunk driving and teen drinking," Blumenthal said in a statement.
"The key is to hold adults accountable for all of the harm caused by their breaking the law."
"The tags and signed receipts would help authorities identify the adults who purchase kegs for parties attended by minors and hold them responsible," Blumenthal said.
"Police need this tool to race the kegs and place the blame where it belongs."at

The tag would include the name, address, and signature of the person who purchases the keg, as well as the purchaser's driver's license number or other identifying information that may be allowed by regulations.
Under the proposed bill, anyone who removes the tag from a beer keg would be subject to up to three months in prison and a fine of up to $500 if convicted.
